environment.note: The challenge text gives 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi (70.3 kPa) or less. Oxygen is capped at 36% (highest design value 34% plus 2 points); the cap is the team's and is not in the challenge text, so a test above 36% oxygen is marked outside the range. Pressure uses the coverage bins around and below 70.3 kPa, because tests set to 0.7 atm are recorded at 70.2 to 72.6 kPa; the range therefore reaches up to 85.8 kPa, above the 70.3 kPa of the bound, and the FLEX tests matched on oxygen and pressure are recorded at 71.2 to 72.4 kPa in the current tables. No flow range is given for this environment. The pair is a bound taken from the challenge statement, which was read from a copy and not checked on the official page; NASA Task Book 14639 names 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia as the most severe test environment (TB14639.worstcase). Nominal values are the bound, not a design point.

needs.reading: A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. The count is not a count of tests that burned, and the lowest oxygen tested is not a flammability limit.
needs.note: The Saffire tables hold one oxygen level near cabin air per test (for Saffire-II derived by NASA from CO2 production, Note 1 of the table), and Saffire-III has no oxygen column. A limit cannot be located from one oxygen level. Pressure is not a required variable of this need, although the cited definition of a threshold holds at a given total pressure, flow and gravity level (ISO16697.threshold): the BASS-II and Saffire tables have no pressure column, so no counted test records a pressure. The BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings are also counted for S1 (Extinction conditions); counts of different needs must not be added.

needs.reading: A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.
needs.note: The one investigation of an extinguishing agent on solid fuels, PSI-26, has an experimental table with sample names only. The counted solid-fuel tests are BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings (extinction, blowoff, no ignition, not sustained); they are also counted for P1 (Flammability limit), and counts of different needs must not be added. Every counted test with added carbon dioxide or helium is a FLEX droplet test. The PSI-69 objective names CO2, He and SF6; the FLEX table has no SF6 column. The other investigations linked to this need add no counted test: PSI-10 and PSI-39 have no column mapped to an outcome variable of this need, and the tables of PSI-20, 21, 23 and 68 are not one row per test.

statements.text: 17 of the 299 tests counted for this need were recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges of this environment.

A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.

The 299 counted tests by match with this environment: 17 with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges; 0 with oxygen inside the range and no pressure in the table; 0 with pressure inside the range and no oxygen in the table; 282 with none of these matches.
The 17 matched tests come from PSI-69.
The 17 matched tests by fuel phase: liquid 17.

Gravity level of the 17 tests with oxygen inside the range and pressure inside the range or not in the table: recorded as lunar, the level of this environment, in 0 tests.

Pressure of the 282 counted tests not matched to this environment: recorded in 256 tests, from 70.1676 to 309.2946 kPa.

The one investigation of an extinguishing agent on solid fuels, PSI-26, has an experimental table with sample names only. The counted solid-fuel tests are BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings (extinction, blowoff, no ignition, not sustained); they are also counted for P1 (Flammability limit), and counts of different needs must not be added. Every counted test with added carbon dioxide or helium is a FLEX droplet test. The PSI-69 objective names CO2, He and SF6; the FLEX table has no SF6 column. The other investigations linked to this need add no counted test: PSI-10 and PSI-39 have no column mapped to an outcome variable of this need, and the tables of PSI-20, 21, 23 and 68 are not one row per test.

references.text: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI): the oxygen mole fraction below which a steady flame cannot exist for a given material and ambient condition. In total flooding, the goal of the agent is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI.
references.title: Research Requirements Document: Droplet Flame Extinguishment in Microgravity (FLEX)
references.quote: For fire safety, the goal of the agent in a total flooding application is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI

references.text: Minimum Extinction Concentration (MEC): the minimum suppressant concentration above which a quasi-steady flame cannot exist. LOI = 0.209 (1 - MEC).
references.title: Research Requirements Document: Droplet Flame Extinguishment in Microgravity (FLEX)

references.text: Objectives: map the flammability boundaries for liquid fuel combustion in reduced gravity; quantify the efficacy of gaseous suppressants over the range of candidate atmospheric pressures and O2 concentrations.
references.title: Research Requirements Document: Droplet Flame Extinguishment in Microgravity (FLEX)

references.text: LOI in oxygen/nitrogen: 0.12 for methanol and 0.15 for heptane; with carbon dioxide dispersed into air at 1 atm: about 0.14 and 0.17.

references.text: ISS response: after detection, ventilation in the affected module is terminated to slow the spread of fire; a portable CO2 extinguisher is used in the U.S. modules.
references.where: ISS Fire Safety Strategy, steps 2 and 5
references.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

references.text: The extinguishing agent must not support combustion in an O2-enriched environment, contain toxic agents, emit toxic products, interfere with visual observation, or be slow to initiate.
references.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

references.text: In BASS-II the flames always quenched when the fan was turned off. The authors call turning off ventilation an excellent mitigation strategy for the ISS, and add that earlier quiescent tests at elevated oxygen suggest ventilation may not be necessary for a flame to survive in high-oxygen low-pressure atmospheres or in partial gravity, so the strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions.
references.title: Flammability Limits from BASS-II Testing in Microgravity Compared to Normal Gravity Limits (Olson, Ferkul, Fernandez-Pello, Miller, Wichman, Bhattacharjee, T'ien)

references.text: SMACs are based on experiments at standard pressure and oxygen. Rev D applies the published ppm values across all atmospheric scenarios, including reduced-pressure exploration atmospheres, for vapor-phase compounds. 1- and 24-hour values apply to off-nominal situations such as accidental releases. The values were established for human spaceflight and are not intended to apply to other situations such as ground operations.

needs.note: Aging time is required, so this need holds the SAME tests of smoke from overheated materials. The smoke-point rows of PSI-107 (gas jet flames: the fuel flow at which the flame starts to emit soot) are a different kind of smoke condition and are not included. The SAME table has four more rows that name Kapton, Silicone Rubber, Lampwick and Dibutyl Phthalate with the words 'same conditions as 1-4' and no values; they are not read. By these words the table treats its columns, the weight loss rate among them, as conditions, while the pipeline lists the mass loss rate as the outcome of this need. The SAME-R rows (PSI-101) hold no mass loss rate and are not counted.
